body:
### Description

Long-running sessions can grow their recorded token usage without a practical upper bound, especially through `tokens.cache.read`, until most models/providers fail with a context-window error and the session becomes unrecoverable.

In my real session, OpenCode reported approximately **56,128,248 total tokens** while the persisted conversation data was small:

```text
session tokens:
  input:        14,774,671
  output:           77,881
  reasoning:        20,400
  cache.read:   41,255,296
  cache.write:           0
  total:        56,128,248

stored rows for that session:
  message: 224 rows, ~0.52 MB JSON data
  part:   1042 rows, ~2.33 MB JSON data
```

After this, continuing the same session fails with:

```text
Your input exceeds the context window of this model. Please adjust your input and try again.
```

The issue is not that the saved message JSON itself is tens of millions of tokens. The large number appears to come from cumulative session usage accounting. In particular, `tokens_cache_read` can grow very large over repeated turns.

Relevant code path observed in source:

```text
packages/core/src/session/projector.ts
  tokens_input:       SessionTable.tokens_input + value.tokens.input
  tokens_output:      SessionTable.tokens_output + value.tokens.output
  tokens_reasoning:   SessionTable.tokens_reasoning + value.tokens.reasoning
  tokens_cache_read:  SessionTable.tokens_cache_read + value.tokens.cache.read
  tokens_cache_write: SessionTable.tokens_cache_write + value.tokens.cache.write
```

This makes session-level usage an ever-growing lifetime counter. That is fine for statistics, but it becomes dangerous if any compaction / routing / provider request / context-window logic treats cumulative session usage, especially `cache.read`, as if it represented the current prompt/context size.

Impact:

- Long sessions eventually hit provider context-window errors.
- Auto compaction does not reliably save an already-overflowed session.
- Once overflowed, the same session can repeatedly fail and effectively becomes unusable.
- `opencode stats` can become slow/hang on large databases/sessions.

comments.author: wang1970
comments.body:
Thanks for the pointers. I checked both suggested issues and I think this report is related but not a straight duplicate.

Clarification:

- #21913 is about **per-assistant-message multi-step accounting** in `processor.ts`: whether fields are overwritten vs accumulated within one assistant message. It explicitly treats `cache.read` as a per-step/session snapshot-like value that should not be summed within one multi-step message.
- This issue is about **session-level persisted counters** in the projector/database growing unbounded across many turns, especially `session.tokens_cache_read`. In my case the stored session row reached:

```text
total ~= 56,128,248
input = 14,774,671
output = 77,881
reasoning = 20,400
cache.read = 41,255,296
```

while the persisted content was only:

```text
message: 224 rows, ~0.52 MB
part:    1042 rows, ~2.33 MB
```

comments.author: wang1970
comments.body:
Bump — this issue has been open for 10 days without any maintainer response.

To add urgency: the unbounded `cache.read` accumulation is not just a cosmetic counting bug. It directly causes **massive token over-consumption** in real usage. Sessions that should have only consumed a few hundred thousand tokens are being accounted as tens of millions, which triggers premature context overflow, failed compaction, and forces expensive re-sends of entire conversation histories.

For anyone hitting the same problem: every long session is silently burning tokens at an inflated rate. This is a **cost and usability regression** that affects all OpenCode users with non-trivial session lengths.

Could a maintainer take a look? The core fix seems straightforward — separate billing/usage totals from effective-context accounting, or exclude `cache.read` from context-window/compaction decisions. Happy t

comments.author: Necmttn
comments.body:
The fix likely needs two counters, not one corrected sum. Keep cumulative billing/usage counters separate from the active context-window counters used for eligibility and compaction decisions.

`cache.read` can be meaningful for cost and provider accounting, but it should not make the next prompt look like it contains 41M active tokens. A good regression would assert that repeated cached turns increase billed/cache usage while active context stays bounded by retained messages plus current tool/schema overhead.

comments.author: AdityaPagare619
comments.body:
Same thing on my end. Session had 937M cache read tokens but only ~41MB of
actual data. The cumulative counter was way out of sync with reality.

This made the context overflow from Bug #3 worse — the session thought it
was already over the limit when the actual context was still manageable.

comments.author: royruho
comments.body:
Confirming this from the user-facing side, and adding a version boundary that may help narrow it.
The additive accumulation described here (session token fields, especially cache.read, summed every turn rather than reflecting current context) appears to be what surfaces as #34712: in Web/Desktop the input/context count is inflated and /compact doesn't bring it down, while the TUI shows the correct current-context number for the same session. That lines up with pruning messages being unable to decrement a cumulative counter.
Version boundary on my end:

1.17.11 — count behaves correctly, no inflation
1.17.12 / 1.17.14 — inflated count, /compact doesn't reduce it

title: Session token usage grows unbounded via cache.read and causes unrecoverable context-window errors
